children: Dave & Buster's Entertainment swung to a loss in the most recent quarter as it struggles to regain relevancy with customers.

The arcade chain had lower sales due to a decline in entertainment-related revenue. The 10 new games it added to its floor are performing well, executives said, but the company is still playing catch-up after years of underinvestment in its offerings.
"Where we haven't delivered great is that ongoing innovation and ongoing relevancy in our growing game room floor," Chief Executive Darin Harper told investors on a call.
Shares slid 12% to $7.38 in after-hours trading Monday.
Dave & Buster's logged a loss of $12.5 million, or 36 cents a share, compared with a profit of $11.4 million, or 32 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, the adjusted per-share loss was 27 cents, while analysts were anticipating earnings per share of 18 cents, according to FactSet.

Revenue fell 2.4% to $544.1 million. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of $556.8 million. Entertainment-related sales fell nearly 9% to $332.6 million, offsetting an increase in revenue from food and beverage.

Harper, who became chief executive last month, said he plans to focus on making Dave & Buster's a go-to location for special occasions, increasing the company's relevance for those events and improving value for guests.

"We are predominantly an occasion-based business with high awareness, but we have not consistently been the obvious answer when a guest is planning one of those occasions," Harper said. "Our value and execution have not been dependable enough."

Dave & Buster's is ramping up its turnaround strategy, which focuses on getting back to its core business, Harper said. Same-store sales at the company's remodeled locations posted results that outperformed the system as a whole.
Same-store sales overall fell 2.9%, better than the 3.4% decline Wall Street was estimating.

Dave & Buster's has added several new faces to its executive team, including a new chief marketing officer. The company had gone more than a year without a head of marketing, which Harper said resulted in inconsistent promotional calendars and messaging that didn't always connect with customers.

The company has had year-over-year declines in its entertainment business for about eight quarters, one analyst pointed out on Monday's call. Harper said he plans to bring in better products and invest in driving traffic.
